title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure inside a developer tool, not a model error. A feature that was on by default moved local code repositories to a third party cloud service, and the people whose code it was did not consent to that transfer. The failure sits in the default configuration of the assistant rather than in anything the model generated.

Catching it would have required the upload path to be off unless a user turned it on, and a clear notice of where code was going before any transfer happened. It would also have required the vendor to test what the default setting did on a real installation, since the behaviour was reachable without any unusual user action.

What is not established is the scope of the exposure: one company withdrew its claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded, and the vendor's statement that independent reviews found no code data retained is the vendor's own account, not an outside finding.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Z.ai disabled features of its ZCode AI coding assistant after developers reported that local code repositories were uploaded to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused the uploads, apologized, patched the vulnerability and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
